context.goal: Reduce resident RAM to break 32B boundary

options_ranked.description: Skip loading FFN_UP dense weights, use INT6 sidecars as primary representation. Makes RAM go down not up.
On-disk derivative format where FFN_UP replaced by sidecar reference. Needs format tooling.
Quantize KV cache to INT8. Measure KV memory at ctx=256/512/1024/2048 for 14B, estimate 32B.
Mark layers as hot/cold. Needs profiling to identify important layers. Requires graph modification.
Already done in Phase 14/15/16. Not a new path, compression overhead already measured.
Audit gguf_init_from_file for lazy-load opportunities. Foundational, long lead time.
Mitigates I/O latency, not primary RAM solution. NVMe ~3-5GB/s, 32B layer ~3-5GB = ~1s/layer.
Stream 1 layer at a time. 32B cold start ~76s even with prefetch. Too slow for real-time.

recommended_phase_18b.name: PRT-Resident Replacement Feasibility Probe
recommended_phase_18b.goal: Determine if FFN_UP tensors can be skipped from GGUF load without breaking model
recommended_phase_18b.approach: 14B probe: load normally, inspect FFN_UP memory fraction, attempt selective skip of FFN_UP init
recommended_phase_18b.what_it_answers: Can we make RAM go DOWN (replace) vs staying flat (add)? If yes, 32B becomes tractable.
recommended_phase_18b.why_14b_not_32b: Tells us what we need without expensive 32B download. Ratio applies equally.
recommended_phase_18b.fallback: KV compression probe or ggml init audit

what_not_to_do: Do not download 32B model on this hardware
Do not generate full 32B sidecar set
Do not claim PRT solves RAM wall yet
Do not mix Phase 18 work with public claims
Do not run long-context 32B without residency confirmed
allowed_claims: RAM wall is primary blocker, not technique
14B is maximum feasible on current hardware until proven otherwise
